about: The Live Lab's pool of real sky samples (tools/extract_slices.py --pool). For each target, a few observations from the Breakthrough Listen Open Data Archive (its queries in order, while it still wants files), or files listed directly. From each file: up to `hits` on-target hits (family stars), the strongest narrowband signals the de-Doppler search finds above `threshold` in one coarse channel (the one containing `freq_mhz`, else up to `tries` drawn at random), and `blind` blind windows (family blind-window) at seeded random frequencies in the first coarse channel read, plus a window centred on each of the target's named `windows` (family stars). The seed fixes every random choice, so re-running the pool cuts the same slices. TRAPPIST-1 and Epsilon Eridani were tried and left out: the archive's TRAPPIST-1 scans have only 3 time steps (a slice needs 16), and it lists no Epsilon Eridani files.

targets.name: Voyager 1
targets.about: Blind windows in the coarse channel of the Voyager scans the voyager slices come from: the 2016 scan and the three 2020 on-source scans. Voyager's own signals stay in the voyager family, as known technosignature controls.

targets.name: Proxima Centauri
targets.about: blc1's window: Parkes (Murriyang) scans of Proxima Centauri from the day blc1 was recorded (2019-04-29), in the coarse channel containing 982.002 MHz, with a window centred on blc1's published frequency in each. Then any Parkes scan of the star.

windows.name: blc1
windows.label: window at blc1's frequency
windows.about: blc1: detected at 982.002571 MHz, drifting +0.038 Hz/s, over about 2.5 hours on 2019-04-29 (Smith et al. 2021, arXiv:2111.08007); shown to be interference (Sheikh et al. 2021)

targets.name: 3I/ATLAS
targets.distance_label: Interstellar comet, the third object seen passing through the Solar System
targets.about: The interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS, observed with Green Bank on 2025-12-18 near its closest approach to Earth: one on-target scan in each of three bands (L, C and Ku). Served over HTTPS by bldata.berkeley.edu.

targets.name: Boyajian's Star (KIC 8462852)
targets.about: The star with the unexplained dips in brightness, from Green Bank's 2018 Kepler-transit session. HTTPS, bldata.berkeley.edu/kepler-transits.

targets.name: Kepler-723
targets.about: A Kepler planet host, from the same 2018 Kepler-transit session. HTTPS, bldata.berkeley.edu/kepler-transits.

targets.name: TIC 265146266
targets.about: A TESS target, observed with Green Bank in 2021. HTTPS, bldata.berkeley.edu/blpd30_datax2.

targets.name: HIP 29847
targets.about: A Hipparcos star, observed with Green Bank in 2021. HTTPS, bldata.berkeley.edu/blpd30_datax2.

targets.name: 'Oumuamua
targets.distance_label: Interstellar object, the first seen passing through the Solar System
targets.about: The first interstellar object found passing through the Solar System, observed with Green Bank at X band in December 2017, weeks after its discovery. HTTPS, bldata.berkeley.edu/pipeline/AGBT17B_999_68.

targets.name: Luyten 726-8 A
targets.about: BL Ceti, the brighter of the Luyten 726-8 pair of red-dwarf flare stars (its companion is UV Ceti), observed with Green Bank at L band in 2016. HTTPS, bldata.berkeley.edu/pipeline/AGBT16A_999_232.

targets.name: Luyten's Star
targets.about: A red dwarf with a planet in its habitable zone (GJ 273 b), observed with Green Bank at L band in 2016. HTTPS, bldata.berkeley.edu/pipeline/AGBT16A_999_214.

targets.name: Gliese 876
targets.about: A red dwarf with four known planets, observed with Green Bank in 2018. HTTPS, bldata.berkeley.edu/pipeline/AGBT18B_999_03.

targets.name: LHS 1140
targets.about: A red dwarf whose rocky planet LHS 1140 b orbits in its habitable zone, observed with Green Bank in January 2017. HTTPS, bldata.berkeley.edu/pipeline/AGBT16B_999_123.

targets.name: Andromeda Galaxy
targets.about: M31, the nearest large galaxy, observed with Green Bank in 2019: one beam takes in a patch of a galaxy of hundreds of billions of stars. HTTPS, bldata.berkeley.edu/pipeline/AGBT19B_999_109.
